claim: Experts recall real game positions far better than novices after a few seconds (about 93% for masters vs about 30-50% for weaker players) and the gap shrinks sharply on random positions.
agent_test: Give the agent domain-valid vs shuffled structured inputs at equal tokens; measure the recall or accuracy gap and check it collapses when structure is scrambled.

claim: A small residual expert advantage on random positions exists (about 5% per 100 rating points on truly random boards), so the Chase-Simon 'no advantage' result reflects tiny N and non-random stimuli.
agent_test: Stratify scrambled inputs and test whether a retrieval memory still gives small gains.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Chunk-based recall is limited to about 3 chunks per recall (not 7) with chunk size up to 15 pieces; within-chunk placement gaps under 2 s; Cowan's 4 may be an overestimate.
agent_test: Measure how many separate items an agent keeps from a long context at equal tokens; compare grouped vs flat context.

claim: Expertise needs a large store of patterns: older indirect estimates run from 10,000 to 100,000 (Simon and Gilmartin) up to 300,000 (Gobet and Simon); a direct archival count gives about 100,000 opening moves for masters; recall rises with the log of stored nodes.
agent_test: Vary size of a retrieval library of domain patterns (10^2 to 10^4) at equal tokens; fit accuracy vs log size.

claim: Templates (chunks with slots) let masters hold up to about 160 pieces over multiple boards with slot filling under 1 s; recall falls with number of boards but trained players plateau.
agent_test: Test schema-with-slots memory entries vs raw text notes on multi-item recall at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Skill advantage on domain memory is moderate across domains: r=.41 overall (games .42, music .69, programming .36, sports .30 ns); after trim-and-fill r=.29, so publication bias may inflate it.
agent_test: Compare memory gain per domain in an agent.

claim: Expert eye movements show fewer fixations (44 vs 84 per trial) with equal fixation duration, and experts find the best move faster (11.7 vs 23.4 s).
agent_test: Test whether an agent that triages salient structure first solves faster at equal tokens.

claim: General intelligence correlates weakly with chess skill (Gf r=.24; youth .32 vs adult .11), so expertise is mostly domain knowledge.
agent_test: Compare a small domain-primed setup with a larger generic one at equal tokens.

claim: Deliberate practice explains a large but limited share of skill variance (games 26%, music 21%, education 4%, professions under 1%); Ericsson's re-analysis gives higher figures.
agent_test: Not directly testable on the agent.

claim: Expertise reversal: novices gain from heavy guidance (d=0.505) while experts do better with less (d=-0.428). LLM analogue (preprints): scaffold uplift tracks headroom (r=0.75) and can regress on a strong target (d07).
agent_test: Vary scaffold strength by task familiarity; test whether heavy scaffolds hurt on familiar tasks at equal tokens.

claim: LLM chess skill degrades sharply outside the training distribution: GPT-5 centipawn loss 26 on familiar positions, no base model beats random on random-piece positions; illegal moves 33.8-74.7% OOD. Only chess measured; a synthetic from-scratch study (abstract only) shows CoT brittleness under shift.
agent_test: Run the scaffold on familiar vs scrambled variants of a task at equal tokens; check it narrows the OOD drop.

claim: More reasoning tokens help in-distribution but give less gain per token on sparse-prior positions; GPT-5 still above 10% illegal moves OOD.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of reasoning length on familiar vs unfamiliar inputs.

claim: Transformers trained on large supervised data reach expert-level chess without search (270M: puzzles 95.4%, blitz Elo 2895 vs humans, 2299 vs bots); pattern knowledge can be amortised.
agent_test: Compare pattern lookup from stored solved cases vs fresh reasoning at equal tokens.

claim: A chess GPT learns board state and a latent skill estimate (probe 99.6% board, 90.5% Elo); a skill intervention raises random-board win rate 16.7 to 43.2% and legal moves to 92%.
agent_test: Suggests priming with skill cues; check at equal tokens.

claim: Expert persona role labels do not improve LLM accuracy (162 personas on 2,410 MMLU questions; six models on GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro; role retrieval no better than no role). Role plus domain facts is untested.
agent_test: Replicate on our agent: persona vs plain at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs simulating novices are poorly calibrated: cosine similarity .16-.19, overconfidence bias +.33 to +.47, AUC near chance.
agent_test: Check the agent's ability to answer as a novice; not core.

claim: Hierarchical working-memory and skill libraries help long-horizon agents: success 42 vs 21%; Voyager 3.3x more items.
agent_test: Test chunked subgoal memory vs flat history at equal tokens.

claim: Reasoning models still fall short of master level in LLM chess (best Elo estimate about 758; 71.9% instruction-following errors for non-reasoning models).
agent_test: Re-run with scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: Scaffold benefit scales with headroom: weak targets gain most (+0.262 vs +0.110), and on a strong target scaffolds regressed in 9 of 20 builder-benchmark cases.
agent_test: Run the scaffold at full and light strength on familiar vs novel tasks at equal tokens; check that light wins when baseline accuracy is high.

claim: A case memory helps only with a quality gate: add-all memory lowered scores (e.g. 55.5 vs 67.5 fixed), strict verified-only addition raised them (70.95), and intermediate memory sizes can beat full memory. No log law was found.
agent_test: Vary library size 0, 10, 100, 1000 with verified-only vs add-all admission at equal tokens; fit gain against log(size).

claim: Chunk count is a noisy metric (test-retest .65 or .36 on game positions, about .14 on random); use accuracy gaps, not chunk counts, as the agent metric.
agent_test: Estimate test-retest of any agent chunk metric over repeated runs before using it.

claim: No study found measuring an LLM game-vs-random recall gap on text tasks; scrambled-text work shows GPT-4 recovers 95% of scrambled sentences, while reordering CJK expressions is hard (12-31% zero-shot).
agent_test: Build matched structured vs shuffled-step inputs (code, proofs, plans) and measure accuracy gap by model size.

claim: Non-chess OOD collapse of the Pleiss type is not yet measured; only a synthetic from-scratch CoT study points the same way.
agent_test: Split a non-chess benchmark into familiar and novel items and compare plain vs scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: Replication of de Groot (6 GMs, 5 IMs, 6 Experts, 5 Class A) kept the pattern-recognition conclusion; AlphaZero learns human-like concepts without human data (probe jump near 32k steps). Neither changes the schema.
agent_test: None needed.
